evidence: The comments at src/sentry/api/paginator.py:179-181 ('allow negative offsets... the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions'), paginator.py:874-876 ('The underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically') and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:26-27 all say negative offsets are supported. They are not. In BasePaginator.get_result (paginator.py:182-184), start_offset = offset whenever cursor.is_prev, and Cursor accepts any int offset (cursors.py:28), so a prev cursor with a negative offset reaches queryset[negative:stop]. The project pins Django 5.2.1 (requirements-frozen.txt:36), and QuerySet.__getitem__ there rejects negative indexes with ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'). The reviewer says AssertionError, which was the behavior in older Django versions; the crash itself is real. Sibling paginators already reject this explicitly with BadPaginationError('Pagination offset cannot be negative') (paginator.py:287, 351, 701, 748, 804). Fix: reject or clamp negative offsets, and remove the misleading comments.

OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key (src/sentry/api/paginator.py:838-840) calls math.floor/math.ceil on getattr(item, self.key). This is copied from the numeric Paginator (paginator.py:222-224). organization_auditlogs.py:76-83 uses it with order_by='-datetime', so the value is a datetime, and math.ceil(datetime) raises TypeError. build_cursor calls get_item_key on every page that has results, so the optimized path fails whenever results exist. value_from_cursor (paginator.py:842-843) also returns the raw int cursor value and compares it against a DateTimeField. DateTimePaginator (paginator.py:230-240) shows the correct conversions (strftime*1000, and fromtimestamp in value_from_cursor).

At src/sentry/api/paginator.py:877-882, when enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, the code slices queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a negative start. organization_auditlogs.py:82 passes enable_advanced_features=True. With Django 5.2.1 (requirements-frozen.txt:36), QuerySet slicing with a negative start raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'). The reviewer says AssertionError, which is the old Django behavior, so a crafted cursor such as '0:-5:0' causes a 500 error. The comment at line 878, 'enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds', also suggests a bounds bypass was intended. Fix: translate negative offsets into positive slices, or reject them with BadPaginationError as the other paginators do (paginator.py:287, 701).

`grep -rln OptimizedCursorPaginator tests/` returns nothing. The diff adds tests only under tests/sentry/spans/ (test_buffer.py, test_consumer.py, test_flusher.py) and none for src/sentry/api/paginator.py:821-912 or the new branch in organization_auditlogs.py:70-83. Tests would have caught both the datetime TypeError (issue 1) and the negative-slice crash (issue 2).

`git diff 28e3db25..HEAD --stat` shows the PR mixes two unrelated changes. The spans buffer work is in src/sentry/scripts/spans/add-buffer.lua, src/sentry/spans/buffer.py and src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/factory.py. The audit-log pagination work is in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py, src/sentry/api/paginator.py and src/sentry/utils/cursors.py. The HEAD commit is even titled 'feat(audit-logs): Enhanced pagination...', which does not match the PR title about spans buffer insertion. Splitting the PR would make review and rollback easier. This is a process concern, not a code defect.
